Find the isopleth level of each event in a utilisation distribution

Source: R/event_ud_level.R
event_ud_level.Rd

This function returns, for each event, the level of the smallest isopleth of a utilisation distribution (UD) that contains its location, i.e. the proportion of the UD in the cells with a density at least as high as the cell of the event. Values near 0 indicate events in the core of the UD; values near 1 indicate events in its periphery (e.g. an event with a value of 0.6 lies outside the 50% home range but inside the 95% one). It is a wrapper around move2utils::ud_outer_probability(), which requires the suggested package move2utils (install it with remotes::install_github("move2universe/move2utils")).

Usage

event_ud_level(x, ud)

Arguments

x

A move2 object.

ud

A UD, either as a terra::SpatRaster (with a layer named ud, or a single layer), or as a tibble of class hr_tt_ud_tbl.

Value

A numeric vector with one value per event of x, between 0 and 1.

Details

ud can be a single UD, used for all events, or a tibble of UDs (of class hr_tt_ud_tbl, as returned by e.g. hr_tt_kde() or hr_tt_dbbmm()). With a tibble, the level of each event is computed in the UD of its own row, matching the first column of the tibble (e.g. the track id) to the column of x with the same name; a tibble with a single row is used for all events.

Events are reprojected to the coordinate reference system of the UD if needed. Events without a location, outside the grid of the UD, or without a matching UD get NA.

Examples

ud <- hr_tt_kde(example_tt)
# the level of each event in the UD of its own track
event_ud_level(example_tt, ud)
#>  [1] 0.37912908 0.20519589 0.02592777 0.24422211 0.46157643 0.12108702
#>  [7] 0.04158419 0.54295652 0.52136846 0.22928935 0.52545507 0.07887490
#> [13] 0.04175892 0.04175892 0.61434549
# the level of each event in the UD of track "a"
event_ud_level(example_tt, ud$ud[["a"]])
#>  [1] 0.37912908 0.20519589 0.02592777 0.24422211 0.46157643 0.99989931
#>  [7] 0.99664072 1.00000000 0.78633036 0.98434300 0.93014376 1.00000000
#> [13] 1.00000000 1.00000000 1.00000000
